title: INFANT Engagement Metrics Glossary
organisation: INFANT Research Centre, University College Cork

usage.authority: Use definitions in this file as the report's approved reference after INFANT review; do not generate replacement definitions.
reporting_rules: Include only glossary entries for metrics actually used in the report.
Display definition and why_it_matters verbatim or without changing their meaning.
Resolve source, time period, unit, aggregation and calculation_method before interpreting a metric.
Never equate impressions or views with unique people, or visibility with demonstrated impact.
If a platform's exported metric differs from this glossary, flag the discrepancy for review.
Do not calculate rates using mismatched periods or denominators.
Append a methodology note stating reporting and comparison periods, sources, missing data and calculation limitations.

metrics.definition: The number of unique accounts that saw content during a defined period, according to the platform's measurement method.
metrics.why_it_matters: Shows the breadth of INFANT's visibility. One account may see multiple posts.
metrics.calculation_notes: Do not sum daily or post-level unique reach and label the result quarterly unique reach; deduplication is required.

platform_notes.Instagram: Accounts reached is an estimated unique-account measure for the selected period; confirm the export's period and definition.
platform_notes.Facebook: Reach may be reported for content or a Page; specify which.
platform_notes.LinkedIn: Check whether the export reports unique impressions/reach or ordinary impressions.

metrics.definition: The number of times content was displayed, including repeat displays to the same account.
metrics.why_it_matters: Shows the volume of exposure, not the number of unique people reached.
metrics.calculation_notes: Add impressions only across non-overlapping periods or disjoint content records; platform definitions can vary.

platform_notes.LinkedIn: Impressions are not the same as unique viewers or members reached.

metrics.definition: The number of times content was viewed or played, according to the platform's definition.
metrics.why_it_matters: Useful for assessing content consumption. A view is not necessarily a unique viewer.
metrics.calculation_notes: Record whether the source refers to post views, video views, plays or page views; these are not interchangeable.

platform_notes.Instagram: Meta's views metric and video-play definitions may change; record the export label and definition.
platform_notes.Facebook: Distinguish content views from Facebook Page views.

metrics.definition: Audience actions such as reactions, comments, shares and saves, as included by the reporting platform.
metrics.why_it_matters: Indicates active responses to content, beyond simply seeing it.
metrics.calculation_notes: Document included actions and avoid adding a total interactions field to its constituent actions.

platform_notes.LinkedIn: Reactions, comments, reposts and clicks may be separate or combined depending on the export.
platform_notes.Instagram: Confirm whether shares and saves are included in the selected interactions measure.

metrics.definition: The percentage of interactions relative to a specified denominator, such as reach, impressions or followers.
metrics.why_it_matters: Helps assess audience response. The denominator must always be stated.
metrics.calculation_notes: Formula: 100 × defined interactions / defined denominator. Never compare rates with different denominators without explanation. If denominator is zero or unknown, do not calculate.

platform_notes.LinkedIn: Native engagement rate may include clicks as well as social interactions; verify the export definition.
platform_notes.Facebook: Page-level engagement rate may use a different denominator than post-level engagement rate.
platform_notes.Instagram: Specify whether calculated by reach, impressions or followers.

metrics.definition: Visits to INFANT's social media profile during the reporting period.
metrics.why_it_matters: May indicate interest in learning more about INFANT.
metrics.calculation_notes: Visits are not necessarily unique visitors; do not infer website visits or link clicks.

metrics.definition: The increase or decrease in followers during a reporting period.
metrics.why_it_matters: Helps assess whether INFANT is developing a sustained audience.
metrics.calculation_notes: Net growth = ending follower count minus starting follower count. New followers is a separate acquisition metric and may not equal net growth; specify which is used.

metrics.definition: Clicks on a link associated with a post, profile or campaign, as defined by the platform.
metrics.why_it_matters: Indicates movement towards another destination, such as a research article or donation page.
metrics.calculation_notes: Distinguish outbound clicks from all clicks, and clicks from confirmed website sessions or conversions.

metrics.definition: Distinct website users estimated by the analytics platform during a defined period.
metrics.why_it_matters: Shows the approximate size of the website audience.
metrics.calculation_notes: GA4 user metrics may distinguish total users and active users; record the exact exported metric.

platform_notes.Google Analytics 4: Reports often display Active users as Users; check the report or API field before labelling.

metrics.definition: Groups of interactions with the website during a visit, as defined by the analytics platform.
metrics.why_it_matters: Indicates how frequently people are using the website.
metrics.calculation_notes: Sessions are not unique people; one person can generate multiple sessions.

platform_notes.Google Analytics 4: Use the GA4 sessions metric and its configured session rules.

metrics.definition: The number of times website pages were viewed, including repeat views.
metrics.why_it_matters: Shows which content attracts attention.
metrics.calculation_notes: Distinguish website page views from Facebook Page views; in GA4, Views may include screen views if app data is included.

platform_notes.Google Analytics 4: Confirm whether the data includes web-only page views or combined page/screen views.

metrics.definition: In Google Analytics 4, sessions lasting longer than 10 seconds, recording a key event, or containing at least two page or screen views, subject to property configuration.
metrics.why_it_matters: Provides a more meaningful measure of website activity than visits alone.
metrics.calculation_notes: GA4's engagement-time threshold may be configurable; verify property settings.

platform_notes.Google Analytics 4: Use the engagedSessions field and confirm configured thresholds.

metrics.definition: The channel through which visitors arrived, such as search, social media or referral.
metrics.why_it_matters: Helps identify which engagement channels drive visitors to INFANT's website.
metrics.calculation_notes: Distinguish first-user acquisition from session acquisition; attribution can differ.

platform_notes.Google Analytics 4: Specify whether source/medium or default channel group is user-scoped or session-scoped.

metrics.definition: Reported email opens divided by delivered emails, multiplied by 100, according to the email platform's method.
metrics.why_it_matters: Indicates readership interest, although privacy protections can inflate recorded opens.
metrics.calculation_notes: Often calculated with unique opens; verify the provider definition. Apple Mail Privacy Protection and other privacy features can distort opens.

metrics.definition: The proportion of delivered emails that generated a recorded link click, according to the email platform's method.
metrics.why_it_matters: Indicates whether readers are taking action. Use the email platform's exact calculation.
metrics.calculation_notes: Common formula: 100 × unique clickers / delivered emails. Verify whether the provider uses unique or total clicks and whether automated security clicks are filtered.

metrics.definition: Unique clickers divided by unique recorded openers, multiplied by 100.
metrics.why_it_matters: Helps assess response among recorded openers, but inherits open-tracking limitations.
metrics.calculation_notes: Formula: 100 × unique clickers / unique recorded openers. Do not calculate when openers are zero or unknown.

metrics.definition: Unsubscribes divided by delivered emails, multiplied by 100.
metrics.why_it_matters: Helps monitor whether content remains relevant to subscribers.
metrics.calculation_notes: Use a consistent campaign-level denominator and verify the email platform's calculation.

metrics.definition: Individual instances of INFANT appearing in media coverage.
metrics.why_it_matters: Measures coverage volume; multiple mentions may relate to the same story.
metrics.calculation_notes: Count each verified outlet/publication instance according to a documented rule; distinguish online and print duplicates.

metrics.definition: Distinct research announcements or topics covered by the media.
metrics.why_it_matters: Helps assess the variety of research receiving attention.
metrics.calculation_notes: Group syndicated and repeated coverage of the same underlying topic under one story identifier.

metrics.definition: Coverage secured through editorial decisions rather than paid placement.
metrics.why_it_matters: Provides an indication of external media interest in INFANT's work.
metrics.calculation_notes: Classify placement type separately from mention counts; exclude advertising and paid sponsored placements.

metrics.definition: A defined action taken after engagement, such as a donation, enquiry or registration.
metrics.why_it_matters: Connects communication activity with measurable outcomes, where tracking is available.
metrics.calculation_notes: Define each conversion event, its source and attribution window; do not assume communications caused the outcome.

metrics.definition: The difference between a metric and the equivalent period in the previous year.
metrics.why_it_matters: Helps account for seasonal patterns when data is comparable.
metrics.calculation_notes: Absolute change = current − prior. Percentage change = 100 × (current − prior) / prior, only when prior is nonzero and metrics are comparable.

metrics.definition: The difference between the current quarter and the preceding quarter.
metrics.why_it_matters: Shows more immediate movement in performance.
metrics.calculation_notes: Absolute change = current − prior quarter. Percentage change = 100 × (current − prior quarter) / prior quarter, only when prior is nonzero and metrics are comparable.
